title: No post-condition assertions on the script's most consequential writes (phUSD mint-authority swap, setMigrator, wiring) — fire-and-forget; a silent partial/incorrect write goes unnoticed at deploy time
description: The script performs its most consequential writes (phUSD mint-authority swap, setMigrator, wiring) without any post-condition assertions that read back and verify the resulting on-chain state matches intent. A silent partial or incorrect write would only be caught later, not at deploy time. This is a defense-in-depth / state-handling gap with no standalone impact; it is made more pointed by the two fork-confirmed ABI drifts (M-01/M-02) on the same script.
impact: No direct or standalone impact. Configuration-safety / state-handling gap (missing verification gate): amplifies other findings but causes nothing alone; requires a separate incorrect write to actually cause harm. C4 Low/QA.
attackPath: Script performs mint-authority swap + setMigrator + wiring.
No post-write assert verifies the resulting on-chain state matches intent.
A misconfiguration would only be caught later, not at deploy time.
recommendation: Add a post-condition epilogue that reads back and asserts each consequential write: phUSD minter == minterV2, migrator == expected, and all wiring fields, with a clear revert on mismatch so any silent/partial write fails loud at deploy time.

evidence.observed: _printSummary logs state but no read-back asserts on the authority swap / setMigrator / wiring.
evidence.amplifiedBy: M-01 / M-02 fork-confirmed ABI drifts on the same script.
